_note: Public record of times this review was wrong. Rendered on the Method tab once populated. Append-only.

entries.where: claude/source-genealogy.md, Tychonian lineage table, Bouw row
entries.old_argument: Cited creation.com/geocentric-gobbledegook as the source for Bouw's concession that his model is observationally equivalent to heliocentrism.
entries.new_argument: That page is Danny Faulkner reviewing Marshall Hall's 'The Earth is not Moving'. It does not support the Bouw concession. Use the Bouw Wikipedia entry and Faulkner's companion article 'Geocentrism and Creation', Journal of Creation 15(2) 2001, which states the essential difference is a coordinate change from Sun to Earth.
entries.reason: Citation checked against the source and did not say what we attributed to it.

entries.new_argument: The PDF paginates 79-81. The quoted concession is on p. 80.
entries.reason: Page range did not match the document.

entries.where: corpus: ARG-C02 originator; and claude/source-genealogy.md by implication
entries.old_argument: Attributed the 16 sun-motion scriptural proof-texts (Joshua 10, Habakkuk 3, Ecclesiastes 1:5, Psalm 19, Isaiah 38) to William Carpenter, One Hundred Proofs (1885).
entries.new_argument: Verified against the full Gutenberg text (143,011 chars): Carpenter's book contains exactly ONE scriptural proof, #50, and it concerns immovability and the stretched-out earth, not the sun's motion. The words Joshua, Habakkuk and Ecclesiastes appear ZERO times in the book. Carpenter's own sun-motion proofs (38, 39) argue from observed appearance. The sun-motion proof-text corpus is a later accretion; C02 reattributed to Rob Skiba's modern biblical-cosmology compilations. C01 (immovability texts) correctly stays with Carpenter.
entries.reason: Attribution asserted from the shape of the genre rather than checked against the primary text.

entries.old_argument: All 15 R06 item titles attributed to Sungenis & Bennett, Galileo Was Wrong Vol. I (2006).
entries.new_argument: Full-text search of the archive.org scan of Vol. I returns ZERO occurrences of 'Noether', 'Fermat', 'light cone'/'lightcone'. 'Gauge' occurs only as Ron Hatch's clock-rate scale factor, not gauge symmetry. 'Renormalization' occurs only as a complaint about QFT infinities, never about frames. 'Anthropic' occurs three times with the authors ATTACKING the anthropic principle, so the item title 'Anthropic coordinate justification' states the REVERSE of the source's stance. At least 6 of 15 item titles are unlocatable in the cited source and are marked as such rather than refuted as the authors' claims.
entries.reason: Cluster-level attribution was applied to every item in the cluster without checking each against the source text.
entries.caveats: The scan is one volume of a multi-volume work; OCR quality is variable; these vocabularies do circulate in downstream forum material. The defensible claim is 'not located in the scanned text of Vol. I', NOT 'the authors never wrote this'.

entries.old_argument: Named the argument "No wind/drag from Earth's motion; atmosphere can't co-rotate" and gave the basis as "Assumes the atmosphere is not gravitationally bound to the Earth. It is."
entries.new_argument: Rowbotham asserts the opposite of what we attributed to him. Earth Not a Globe grants co-rotation outright - "we are compelled to conclude that if the earth revolves, the atmosphere revolves also, and in the same direction" - and argues from inside that concession that no residual effect is felt. Renamed "No wind or drag is felt from the Earth's motion"; basis now answers the real claim via Coriolis deflection. Originator year corrected 1865 to 1881: the atmospheric argument enters with the enlarged 3rd edition.
entries.reason: We refuted the list's one-line fragment instead of the source's sentence, and the fragment states the reverse of the source. This is precisely the failure the hedge rule was introduced to catch, and it was the first thing the rule caught.

entries.old_argument: Both refutations argue against the list's fragments artefact by artefact - GPS, sextants, ephemerides for R08; Noether, Fermat, light cones, gauge symmetry for R06.
entries.new_argument: Neither argument form appears in the cited source. Both refutations have been rewritten. R08 now answers the book's conventionalism first - the Einstein/Infeld sentence with its governing condition restored, and the reply that a conventional choice of origin is not a conventional choice of dynamics - and reaches the 28 artefacts only afterwards, under a heading stating they are the list's addition and not the authors'. R06 now concedes the one sentence the source does supply, states the six unlocatable item titles WITH the caveats (one scanned volume, variable OCR, unresolved volume identity, search not independently re-run) before refuting anything, leaves the anthropic reversal unsettled given Woit's contrary testimony, and addresses the remaining items as claims of unknown authorship. Regression tests pin all of it.
entries.reason: Same failure as A10, caught by the same audit. Recording it before fixing it, because a review about provenance should not be able to correct itself silently. Fixed same week; the A10 headline and TLDR were found to carry the same mis-attribution and were rewritten with them.

entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-A05 - originator year AND published basis line
entries.old_argument: Credited to Zetetic Astronomy: Earth Not a Globe, 1865, with the basis line 'Rowbotham took his pseudonym from the thing he denied.'
entries.new_argument: Both wrong. The parallax argument is NOT in the 1865 edition - 'parallax' occurs there twice, both times in the byline - it is an 1881 third-edition addition, ch. III pp. 82-87. And the pseudonym line is false: Rowbotham was signing himself 'Parallax' by the end of 1849, 32 years before he wrote about stellar parallax, in the generic optical sense (apparent shift with viewpoint) that his own perspective theory depends on. He relied on parallax, he did not name himself after a thing he denied. Line withdrawn and replaced.
entries.reason: A rhetorically attractive line that did not survive checking. Those are the ones most likely to be wrong, which is why it was checked.

entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-B04 - originator year and basis line
entries.old_argument: Credited to Zetetic Astronomy 1849. Basis said Carpenter's proofs 5 and 36 (Cape Hatteras, Chesapeake Bay) reappear as Dubay's 89 and 96.
entries.new_argument: 1849 is impossible: the ancestral passage cites the Port Nicholson light, erected 1859, and the lighthouse table is absent from the 1865 first book edition. It is an 1881 third-edition addition, ch. II pp. 28-35. On the basis line, proof 36 to Dubay 96 holds, but Dubay's 89 is Cape Agulhas and 'Cape Hatteras' does not occur in 200 Proofs at all; Carpenter's proof 5 survives instead in a 2018 Dubay blog post. The lighthouse spine of the cluster is Rowbotham's table, not Carpenter's - the reverse of what the old line implied.
entries.reason: Edition dating never checked against the primary text; a lighthouse erected in 1859 cannot appear in an 1849 pamphlet.

entries.old_argument: Both items credited to Rowbotham, Zetetic Astronomy, 1849.
entries.new_argument: Item 42 is Rowbotham's. Item 384 (river grades) is not: it is absent from the 1849 pamphlet as quoted by Schadewald, 'Nile' does not occur in the 1865 text, and the 1881 General Index has no entry for Nile, Rivers, Amazon or Mississippi. Earliest documented text is Carpenter 1885 proof 4 - 'the Nile, which, in a thousand miles, falls but a foot' - passing near-verbatim into Dubay's proof 5.
entries.reason: We inherited the attribution from the movement's own genealogy rather than checking the primary text. Third instance of this failure mode.

entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-D07 - basis line, originator order and year
entries.old_argument: Basis said: "Blavatsky's claimed source text, the 'Book of Dzyan', is regarded by Buddhist-studies scholars as her own invention." Credited to Blavatsky first, Isis Unveiled, 1877.
entries.new_argument: The Dzyan sentence is withdrawn entirely. It is wrong on three counts: the Stanzas frame The Secret Doctrine (1888), not Isis Unveiled (1877), which is the work this cluster was dated to; the people on record treating it as fabricated are a historian, a 19th-c. critic and a writer on fringe claims, not Buddhist-studies scholars, while the one long-term Sanskrit and Tibetan-Buddhist specialist on the question, David Reigle, reports circumstantial evidence in FAVOUR of authenticity; and no item in the cluster descends from Dzyan in any case. Separately, the twelve items track Hall's 1928 chapter list almost one-for-one, so Hall is the primary originator and the year is 1928.
entries.reason: MAJOR under our own review rules: an unsourced bad-faith attribution, made in the name of a scholarly field that says close to the opposite. It was also irrelevant to every item in the cluster, which is how it survived unchecked.

entries.old_argument: Said the maxim was 'popularised in its modern form by a 1908 Chicago New Thought pamphlet.'
entries.new_argument: Overcredits the Kybalion. The compact English axiom was already free-standing in Blavatsky's Isis Unveiled (1877) - 'As above, so it is below... As in heaven, so on earth.' The Kybalion's contribution was to codify it as one of seven numbered Principles, not to popularise it. Wording corrected.
entries.reason: Precision, not a reversal - but on a page whose product is provenance, 'popularised by' and 'codified by' are different claims about who did what.
